title: One step of the read sweep
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $E$ inject the symbols of $\Gamma$ together with blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits, and let $e$ embed the binary alphabet into $\Gamma$. For a machine $M$ over $\Gamma$, a binary input $x$, a configuration $c$ of $M$ on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$, a state $q$ of $M$, and a counter $j\in\{0,\ldots,N+1\}$ with $j<N+1$, one step of the binary block-code simulator from the read-sweep configuration at counter $j$ is the read-sweep configuration at counter $j+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is an embedding of symbols and blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits
$M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$
replaced:
For a counter $j \le N$, one transition of the binary block-code simulator applied to
the read-sweep configuration of a source configuration $c$ with source state $q$ at
counter $j$ yields the read-sweep configuration at counter $j+1$: the scanned code bits
enter the buffers and every work head moves one cell right.
